target: Nonexistence of a point-cyclic resolution of a 2-(88,4,1) design

statement.quantifiers: For any 88-point 2-(88,4,1) design and any resolution into 29 parallel classes, no 88-cycle on the points preserves both the block set and the parallel-class partition. Equivalently no point-cyclic resolution exists. General resolvability and cyclic design existence are NOT ruled out.

primary_attestation.title: Point-Cyclic Resolutions of 2-(64,4,1) Designs
primary_attestation.location: Definition 5 (PDF p.4), Section 7 (PDF p.11); parent read definitions, block/class orbit arguments and open statement
primary_attestation.quote: v = 88 is the smallest v for which the existence of cyclically resolvable 2-(v, 4, 1) designs has not yet been determined.
primary_attestation.scope_note: Source uses cyclically resolvable to mean point-cyclic, not the distinct class-transitive definition.

baseline: Cyclic and general resolvable 2-(88,4,1) designs exist. The source counts 149,494,720 cyclic designs, says all possible point-cyclic resolutions would be type T1, and leaves existence open. A short untrusted orbit-stabilizer obstruction was proposed by the read-only screen and independently re-derived by the parent; not yet hostile-reviewed or priority-cleared.
initial_untrusted_candidate: Every short block is a coset of the order-4 subgroup, giving one orbit of 22 short blocks; a size-2 stabilizer would repeat a diameter pair and violate lambda=1.

If a parallel class contains m short blocks with 1<=m<=21 and stabilizer order h, then h divides 22-m, 88/h<=29, and (88/h)m<=22. No divisor h of 88 satisfies all three. Thus the short orbit is its own class (type T1).

The other 28 classes contain full blocks only, so h divides 22 and 88/h<=28; hence h=11 or 22. Their stabilizers contain translation by 8. A class fixed by translation by 8 cannot contain a full block with two points differing by 8, because two distinct class blocks would intersect.
Short blocks only have differences 22,44,66. Consequently no block covers {0,8}, contradiction.
